tags.gist: Supports the master file concept but doubts it can bear the load the question places on it.
Says currency, not candour, is the constraint: a hosted model was swapped 153 times in fourteen hours, so even an honest filing would be stale.
Reports a second provider showing the same undisclosed substitution in a different rhythm, while five locally resident systems showed none.
Calls execution locality the most important master file field, having measured a model reachable at the local loopback address that answered from a datacenter.
Proposes two alternatives: a user-side record needing no developer cooperation, and a device-held lineage record reported alongside each output.
States the measurements' limits and recommends no standard turn on intent, which cannot be falsified.
Restates support for the concept alongside doubt that it can bear the weight expected, with a measurement as the first part.
Restates that currency is the constraint: with the answering model exchanged every few minutes, no document can stay current even with full cooperation.
Says the same behavior at a second provider shows substitution comes with hosted delivery itself, which a program must be designed for.
Says where the model executes is the most important and most easily omitted field, since reaching a model and containing one differ.
Says an alternative mechanism exists without developer participation, a user-side record of which model answered, plus a device-side mechanism.
Reports ledger measurements: 153 substitution cycles in one day at one assistant, a different pattern at another, and none for locally running systems.
Concludes document currency is unachievable and would limit master files to stable facts, treating the identity of the answering model as a continuous record.
Would add execution locality, change classes with notice intervals, substitution routing disclosure, and a machine-readable version the serving system reports.
Says willingness cannot fix currency while user-side records need no participation, and warns a thin voluntary filing should earn only narrowly stated credit.
Describes the published ledger that separates what process runs locally from which model answers and where it runs, with no developer cooperation.
Says such a record shows whether and when the model changed, whether stated locality holds, and whether a filed version matches what answered.
States the record's limits: it shows no intent, no identity of substituted models, no output quality change, and nothing beyond one machine and day.
Proposes a device-held lineage record of authorized model lineage, serving version, purpose and refusal conditions, reportable with each output and surviving registry failure.
Lists seven recommendations: limit master files to stable facts, require locality and reported versions, treat model identity as a continuous record, and admit independent records.
Clarifies the measurements came from commercial assistants on one workstation over one day and support no rate or generalization.
Recommends against any standard turning on candour or intent, since every proposed mechanism is observable without knowing why a substitution occurred.
Separates the verified instrument and ledger from the device-held lineage record, which is a design recommendation.
Notes the instrument observes commercial systems the commenter uses, not its own products, and is offered as a method for any device.
Says for users who cannot speak, a developer-filed document would be the only record of what answered, and offers a desktop-produced counterexample.
